posts.author: Piyan Glupak
posts.body:
Are these 'A' sheet tiles? The A1, A2, A3 and A4 sheets are for autotiles, which means that each tile that you see in the database actually consists of several tiles.
The idea with autotiles is that the developer doesn't have to worry which particular tile to use for edges or corners, because the RPG Maker program does it for them. [There is a very easy way to overide the program's choice, by the way.]
It might be a good idea to have a good look at the MV help file, particularly "Asset Standards", "Tileset Details".

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
Basically there are six different formats for tilesheets (A1 to A5 and the sixth for B-E), and each format only functions correctly in their specific slots.
And by "format" I DON'T mean png, I mean pixel size and positions of different tiles (regular tiles, wall autotiles, regular autotiles, animated autotiles - going from 48x48 over 96x144 to 288x144pixel per tile).
All formats are described under asset standards in the help file
